newsitem.title: ST VINCENT: CRICKET-CAMPBELL AND WILLIAMS PUT WINDIES BACK ON TRACK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CAMPBELL AND WILLIAMS PUT WINDIES BACK ON TRACK.

text.p: Openers Sherwin Campbell and Stuart Williams spearheaded a West Indies revival on rain-shortened third day of their second test against Sri Lanka on Sunday.
Williams made 46 and Campbell 33 as West Indies made good their 75-run first innings deficit to end the day on 128 for two, 53 runs ahead.
Only just over two hours of play was possible because of a heavy downpour during the afternoon and at the close Brian Lara was unbeaten on 30 and left-hander Floyd Reifer on 15.

West Indies, who lead the two-match series 1-0, batted aggressively after resuming at 19 without loss. Despite losing both Campbell and Williams, they added 105 runs in the morning session but rain during the lunch interval left pools of water on the ground.
Lara, with just five runs in three innings against the Sri Lankans, struggled with his timing early on but looked to be returning to form before bad light finally ended play for the day.
The adventurous Campbell was first to fall with the score on 62, paying dearly for being overly attacking.
He struck six fours in his cameo knock, two coming in the space of four balls from fast bowler Ravindra Pushpakumara, but was bowled when he attempted a forcing back foot drive.
Williams executed a couple of exquisite back foot drives off both Pushpakumara and left-arm paceman Sanjeewa de Silva but was also dropped at 38 when de Silva floored a return catch.
He moved to within four runs of a half-century with consecutive boundaries off de Silva but in the next over spinner Muttiah Muralitharan had him caught at silly point by Sanath Jayasuriya.
